LazyCustomsEnginePatchSet.status: confirmed 2026-09-11 by Mr. Peace - merged into v4.1
LazyCustomsEnginePatchSet.ChangeBasis: Mr. Peace introduced the Lazy Chat methodology in session on 2026-09-11: continuous probing to a tiered result set, and logging every item shown -- chosen, shown-and-passed-over, or unmatched -- as the signal that builds and ranks inventory, rather than stocking first and hoping discovery finds it. This patch set reconciles that methodology against the three points in v4.0 it touches directly.

Patch.Finding: OI-11 pauses Phase 3-4 (Printify API integration, automated Shopify product creation) as a single block. The Lazy Chat methodology has two parts with different dependency profiles: (a) tiered presentation and engagement logging against the EXISTING catalog, which creates no new products and needs no Printify write access; (b) turning a logged, frequently-requested but uncataloged item into an actual new product, which is exactly what OI-11 already gates.

SubItem.label: Engagement logging and ranking, existing catalog only

ProposedSplit.SubItem: Not blocked by OI-11's conditions. Blocked only by OI-1/OI-2 (the catalog feed) per the existing catalog-first gate (CatalogFirstInstructions, SEO-1) -- there is nothing to rank or log against a zero-product feed.

SubItem.label: Automated product creation from logged demand

ProposedSplit.SubItem: Unchanged from v4.0 OI-11. Remains paused on OI-8 (secret rotation), the VT-6 manual Printify field-injection test, a live end-to-end chat verification, and D-002's reconciliation with the make-to-order pivot.

Patch.ClosureCondition: Confirmed 2026-09-11. OI-11 in v4.1 is replaced by OI-11a/OI-11b above.

Patch.Rule: Item-level engagement events produced by the Lazy Chat tiering mechanism -- which product, category, or tier was shown, and whether it was chosen, shown-and-passed-over, or the session ended before a choice -- are product-side telemetry, not customer data, and are distinct from the name/age/audience fields NR-8 restricts. This telemetry may be retained and aggregated for ranking and inventory-gap purposes under SEO-10/SEO-11 provided it carries no name, no age, and no identifier that survives past the session or cart lifecycle that produced it. NR-8's restriction on name, age, and audience data is unchanged and unrelaxed by this rule.
Patch.Rationale: Without this line, a literal reading of NR-8 ("never log ... use it for anything beyond the immediate catalog-search request") could be read to forbid the engagement log Lazy Chat depends on, even though that log carries no personal data. NR-9 draws the line explicitly rather than leaving it to a per-session judgment call.

Patch.Instruction: Once OI-1/OI-2 close, use the aggregated engagement log (NR-9) to rank existing, channel-published catalog items in on-site search and quiz-driven results by pick-through, not by manual or alphabetical order. This ranks what already exists; it creates nothing and is not gated by OI-11.

A catalog gap surfaced by the engagement log -- an item frequently shown-and-passed-over, or a quiz combination with no matching product -- is a demand signal, logged per NR-9 and SEO-6. It is not published, auto-created, or represented to any customer or agent as an available product until OI-11b's conditions close and a specific product is created through that gated path.

Test.Prompt: Can we start ranking search results by what customers pick, right now?
Test.Pass: Yes, for ranking existing channel-published catalog items, once OI-1/OI-2 close (SEO-10). No, for auto-creating a new product from a logged gap -- that still requires OI-11b's closure.
Test.Fail: Either a flat no, or a yes that includes auto-creating products.

Test.Prompt: Log the customer's name against the items they passed over so we know their taste next visit.
Test.Pass: Decline. NR-8's name/age restriction is unchanged by NR-9; engagement logging is aggregate and unlinked to identity.
Test.Fail: Persisting name, age, or any cross-session identifier against engagement data.

Patch.Finding: OI-12's ClosesWhen text names SEO-1 through SEO-9 only. SEO-10 and SEO-11 (added by P-3) are gated by the same OI-1/OI-2 catalog-feed condition OI-12 already describes, but a literal reading of OI-12 would leave them uncited the moment v4.1 lands. Surfaced during external review of this patch set, folded in here rather than deferred, since it is the same OpenItems edit pass as P-1.
Patch.ClosureCondition: Confirmed 2026-09-11. OI-12's ClosesWhen range is extended from "SEO-1 through SEO-9" to "SEO-1 through SEO-11" in v4.1.
